title: Star brightness
info: Apparent magnitude is how bright a star looks from Earth. A smaller number means brighter.
The Sun is about magnitude -27. The full Moon is about -13. Sirius, the brightest night star, is about -1.5. The faintest stars most people can see are about magnitude 6.
Absolute magnitude imagines every star at the same distance, so you can compare real power.
A star can look bright because it is close, truly luminous, or both.
